title: Biographical details; family and work history
description: Interviewer Isabel Miller records Sonja Christine Clyne's name, birth date of May 12, 1953, Elk River address, and maiden name Ohlson. Sonja identifies her husband Wayne Klein, a truck driver born in Princeton, Minnesota, and their son Eric, then recounts her medical assistant training in San Francisco, bookkeeping at BMW Excavating, and nursing work for Dr. Brieger at Potlatch.

title: Hobbies; clubs; small town versus city life
description: Sonja describes fixing hair, chairing the Miss Elk River pageant, and her Canasta birthday club, and the interviewer tells of planning a party for Norma in Deary. Sonja then explains why she prefers Elk River over San Francisco, where she found the city unsafe and lonely despite making one good friend.

title: Living and volunteering in San Francisco; city encounters
description: Sonja recalls living with a family in San Francisco, babysitting and keeping house for forty dollars a month, and volunteering at St. Ann's home taking residents for walks. She recounts frightening city experiences including a stranger inviting her to a party at a stoplight and unfriendly bus drivers, contrasting this with helpful Elk River neighbors.

title: Medical needs and skills in Elk River
description: Sonja explains how her medical assistant training lets her give injections locally, such as monthly allergy shots, since Elk River has no doctor or nurse. She discusses borrowing supplies from Dr. Drury in Troy and wishes a doctor would visit town regularly for blood pressure checks and other care.

title: Family life, childhood play, and girls' athletics
description: Sonja compares her son Eric's upbringing with her own, describing camping, fishing, and neighborhood barbecues in Elk River. She recalls playing baseball with her brother Johnny and describes how girls at her high school won basketball only in her senior year after persistent pressure and the help of teacher Mrs. Molesy.

title: Education and family expectations
description: Sonja discusses her parents' mixed feelings about her going to San Francisco for school and her interest in speech pathology. She contrasts her own success with her brother Johnny, who was defeated by teachers' low expectations, and her brother Jeff, whose mechanical talent the family hopes to develop.

title: Returning to Elk River; courtship and marriage
description: Sonja observes that people who leave Elk River usually come back because family ties are strong there. She tells how she met her husband Wayne through a girlfriend while he worked on the fire patrol, decided to marry him the first night, and says marriage has made her happier than ever.

title: Medical services; children and their upbringing
description: Sonja and Isabel discuss the insecurity of having no doctor in town, especially in winter and for elderly people without cars. Sonja says she wants two children, values her mother's and grandmother's help with Eric, and criticizes mothers who push early potty training and compare their babies.

title: Recreation; family outings
description: Sonja describes weekends with Wayne and Eric, including picnics, water skiing, and walks in the woods, with occasional trips to Moscow for a show. She expects her small family will do more things together than her own family did, since her brothers were so different in age.

title: Social life and recreation; risk of husband's injury
description: Sonja Clyne talks about taking her son Eric along on family outings, the limited recreation in Elk River such as the bar and pool tournaments, and socializing with other mothers. She discusses her fear of Steve being hurt driving, a friend whose husband was killed, and how Steve would struggle if she had to support the family.

title: Finding work; Depression lessons; credit and debt
description: Sonja describes the difficulty of finding a job after school and how her experience would help now. She and Isabel Miller discuss advice from the Depression generation, their shared dislike of credit and finance companies, and Isabel's story of a costly secondhand TV purchase and borrowing money early in her marriage.

title: Depression hardship and the Elk River forest fire; church and Elk River Days
description: Isabel Miller recalls scraping to pay for a washing machine while pregnant with Norma, living in a small rented shack, and the big forest fire when her husband fought fires at night. Sonja then describes attending the Catholic Church in Bovill and the work of putting on the annual Elk River Days festival.

title: Adjusting to Elk River life; entertainment and pastimes
description: Sonja considers what a friend from San Francisco would need to adjust to living in Elk River, including long winters, power outages, logging trucks, and bad roads, and says the town is welcoming to friendly newcomers. She discusses self-entertainment like embroidery and cards, occasional magazines, and her favorite TV shows.

title: Marital decisions; city versus small-town life; contentment as a homemaker
description: Sonja explains how she and Steve make decisions together, manage money, and came to settle in Elk River for his forestry job. She contrasts herself with local girls who never went away to school, saying they idealize city life, and closes by saying she is happy being a wife, mother, and homemaker.
